_about: Public wording for the House as Power Station Provider Explorer. Prepared 13 October 2026 under the founder's instruction to resume the electricity-export Provider Explorer (verified, current official evidence; no rankings, recommendations, rates, earnings or implied partnerships). For founder review before publication. Every sentence cites the supplier's own page AND the verbatim quote(s) it rests on (s = source codes, q = quote keys). ts = time-sensitive: withheld once its evidence is more than 90 days old.

tabs.label: Electricity suppliers
tabs.note: Under Ireland's Clean Export Guarantee, electricity suppliers are required to offer payment for eligible exported electricity, subject to the applicable rules. These are four that PlotNua has checked, not a complete list. The four suppliers listed here require customers to purchase their electricity from them to receive export payments under their published arrangements.

offers.t: Pays its own customers for the electricity their home exports, as a credit on each bill in line with the billing cycle.

how.t: To be paid, the home needs a smart meter, and ESB Networks must have been told about the export connection on an NC6 form.
Where a home is not eligible for a smart meter, Electric Ireland says it pays on a deemed export calculation instead.
It describes its rate as variable and subject to change.

offers.t: Pays its own electricity customers for exported electricity under its Microgen Export Plan, as a credit to the electricity bill.

how.t: A home that is eligible for a smart meter must have one installed, and ESB Networks must have received an NC6 or equivalent form.
A home that is not eligible for a smart meter is paid on a deemed amount, calculated by formula.
Payments start after at least three months of export. Its page gives the frequency as four times a year in one place and every six months in another, so confirm it with Bord Gáis Energy.
It says its rate is subject to change.

offers.t: Credits exported electricity to the bill of a household whose import and export are both with Energia, on the two-monthly bill, as a credit rather than a bank transfer.

how.t: A smart meter is needed to join, and Energia says it can request one. The NC6 form must be submitted to ESB Networks, which an installer may do.
Readings are taken every thirty minutes, and Energia notes that the export period on a bill can differ from the import period.

offers.t: Credits excess exported electricity to a household's Flogas electricity account every two months, with a statement showing whether the credit was metered or deemed.

how.t: The household must be registered with Flogas for its import electricity, and ESB Networks must have been informed on an NC6 or equivalent form.
A home that is eligible for a smart meter but does not have one is not eligible. A home not currently eligible for one is paid on a deemed amount calculated by ESB Networks.
Flogas reserves the right to vary its rate and says it gives thirty days' notice of a change by email or letter.
